text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Streaming route /v1/stream/generate experiencing elevated tail latency and intermittent stalls. p95=1.12s p99=3.24s error-rate elevated. Potential SLO breach. Auto-ticket #INC-26543 created. @oncall-mike please acknowledge :rotating_light:
oncall-mike: acked. i'm on it, looking at graphs now. can someone post the recent deploy history?
eng-runtime: we had a prefix-hash rollout ~15m ago (deploy: prefix-rollout-2026-03-15-001). rollout touched the streaming cache key normalization logic.
sre-nina: seeing a sharp drop in prefix-cache hit rate correlated with the deploy. hit-rate for prefix-cache: 72% -> 18% on the streaming fleet. eviction rate spiked.
eng-runtime: yep, metrics match. logs show a bunch of 404s from cache-read for new prefixes. suspect hash variant mismatch between writer and reader.
cs-jordan: receiving customer reports: three customers reported streaming stalls and socket resets, one reported truncated outputs. escalated to CS manager.
product-olivia: can we do a targeted rollback of the prefix-hash change? prioritise streaming routes only if possible. customers affected are on prod-us-west.
ops-lee: quick mitigation option: enable cache-bypass fallback for streaming route so it fetches from origin and streams, avoiding prefix lookup. less efficient but reduces stalls.
oncall-mike: starting triage steps: 1) pin streaming route to prior model variant 2) enable cache-bypass 3) start rollback canary to 10% for prefix-hash change. posting commands.
eng-runtime: canary rollback command (k8s rollout) below — doing canary to 10% on streaming service:
```
# scale down new rs and scale up old rs for streaming-service
kubectl -n production scale deployment streaming-service-v2 --replicas=1
kubectl -n production scale deployment streaming-service-v1 --replicas=9
```
sre-nina: also running a quick redis inspect to confirm key namespaces. snippet: 
```
# redis sample
redis-cli -h cache-usw1 INFO keyspace
redis-cli -h cache-usw1 --scan --pattern "prefix:*" | wc -l
```
incident-bot: NOTE: rolling back prefix-hash change will cause cache miss storm until warmed. consider gradual canary with monitoring.
eng-runtime: starting canary rollback now (10%). enabling cache-bypass for /v1/stream/generate via feature-flag service.
eng-runtime: feature-flag command: `ff toggle streaming_prefix_cache_bypass --on --scope=us-west --reason="mitigation for prefix-hash regression"`
oncall-mike: executing commands now. monitoring p95/p99 in datadog dash: https://dashboards.redwood/d/streaming/slo-triage
sre-nina: update: after enabling cache-bypass, error spikes reduced, p99 _down_ to 1.8s from 3.2s. still above SLO but much better. hit-rate shows synthetic fills increasing.
cs-jordan: customers confirmed reduced failures for two of three affected accounts. one still seeing reconnects intermittently.
eng-runtime: investigating the remaining reconnects — looks like a small subset of requests still hitting new prefix keys that were hashed differently in the last deploy (edge mismatch). planning to expand canary rollback to 40% while watching eviction pressure.
ops-lee: note we should throttle background batch prefetch to avoid origin overload during warmup. change below: `prefetch_workers=4 -> 1` in runtime config and restart prefetchers.
eng-runtime: applied throttle to prefetchers on canary nodes.
incident-bot: METRICS: p95=0.98s p99=1.42s error-rate trending down. TTL expiry events still elevated but decreasing.
product-olivia: good. start preparing post-incident notification template for impacted customers. include root cause hypothesis: prefix-hash variant incompatibility from recent deploy; mitigation: rollback and cache-bypass; follow-ups needed.
oncall-mike: summary for handoff -> rolling canary to 40% done, cache-bypass enabled in us-west, prefetch throttle applied, monitoring link: https://dashboards.redwood/d/streaming/slo-triage, logs tail: https://logs.redwood/streaming/2654321000. action items for next oncall: 1) complete full rollback if canary stable 2) validate cache warmup and run controlled prewarm sweep 3) run canary traffic replay to ensure no residual mismatch 4) coordinate with CS for customer outreach.
sre-nina: adding retention item: capture a sample of mismatched keys and compare hashing outputs between v1 and v2 for formal root cause. saved sample to /tmp/prefix_mismatch_2654321000.log
cs-jordan: CS will send interim note to impacted customers that we mitigated streaming stalls and are working on a complete rollback and postmortem.
ops-lee: I put an alert to mute noisy eviction alerts for 30m so oncall can focus on p99.
oncall-mike: handing off to @oncall-next (Tiffany) in 30 minutes. leaving runbook: revert id prefix-rollout-2026-03-15-001 (if canary stable) and do full rollout reverse.
eng-runtime: will prepare a cherry-picked patch to unify hash variant and run tests in staging before re-deploy.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, SLO delta reduced. keep thread open for postmortem.
oncall-mike: thanks team. final note for handoff: estimated customer impact window ~15m-45m, affected customers contacted. next oncall please confirm full rollback or safe re-release after root cause fix. :white_check_mark:
